bull_bear.body: Priority 1: Organic growth (Sales & Marketing for CARBON); Priority 2: Maintaining cash reserves for volatile market/inorganic opportunities; Priority 3: No dividends/buybacks mentioned; Cash balance INR 155cr retained for strategic flexibility.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Middle East crisis prolongation impacting SupTech government budgets/pipelines (monitoring post-June); Regulator caution on public AI adoption for confidential data; Execution risk in scaling MSME loan aggregation; Competitive intensity from AI-native entrants (currently low).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously Optimistic; Disciplined on capital allocation; Strategic focus on recurring revenue quality over sheer volume; Watchful on geopolitics but confident in product moat.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management is developing 'sovereign/private LLM' solutions to bypass regulator reluctance on public cloud AI for sensitive financial data; Days receivable improved to 75-80 days due to regulator payment discipline, a rare positive in government-facing businesses.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin held at ~14% by balancing SupTech profits against rising SaaS sales/marketing spend; S&M spend ratio currently 1.1-1.2x net ARR (below industry benchmark of 2.0x), with room to increase aggressively for CARBON growth without breaching EBITDA positivity.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Targeting INR 500cr revenue in 4-5 years (~30% CAGR); Margin: Committed to remaining EBITDA positive while scaling SaaS; Order Inflow: SupTech expecting 3-4 regulator wins/year; Capex/Commissioning: Measured spend on sales/marketing (S&M ratio ~1.1-1.2x ARR) and AI product development.

outlook.body: SupTech pipeline includes Government of Qatar (tax reporting) and ongoing discussions with Middle East regulators; RegTech seeing strong ARR growth (33% for CARBON, 17% for iDEAL) driven by enterprise wins and ESG module adoption.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Geographic expansion of iDEAL into Africa/Middle East/Europe; ESG reporting module upsell; AI-driven features (private/sovereign LLMs) for regulators; Potential inorganic acquisitions in RegTech adjacencies using INR 155cr cash reserve.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: IRIS RegTech posted steady 23% FY26 revenue growth with a strengthened balance sheet (INR 155cr cash) post-TaxTech divestment, pivoting capital toward aggressive SaaS ARR expansion (targeting 35% CAGR) and AI-enabled product enhancements. The strategic shift prioritizes high-margin recurring revenue in global disclosure management while maintaining SupTech as a cash-flow stabilizer, though Middle East tensions pose a monitored risk to government project pipelines.

open.item: Deploy the strengthened balance sheet and liquidity from the divestment into core growth areas - SupTech, RegTech, enterprise SaaS, ESG reporting and international expansion.
Scale the product-led business, improve recurring revenue, strengthen global customer acquisition and enhance operational efficiency.
Management flagged that near-term margins may continue to reflect growth investments in product development, technology, sales and marketing and talent.
Embed artificial intelligence across the product portfolio and shift regulatory reporting from a compliance exercise to an insight-driven process.
Grow the Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) business at 35% year on year.
Keep sales and marketing spend on net new ARR for the year notably lower than the industry standard.
Grow the SupTech and IRIS iDEAL businesses profitably so that the higher sales and marketing spend in IRIS CARBON is compensated to an extent.
Bring in an automated AI-driven iXBRL generation tool, extending the IRIS Instant AI-driven XBRL generation tool launched in May 2025.
Achieve AI fluency across the software development and testing process to sustain productivity gains and shorten feature release cycles.
Develop corporate tax returns as a further regulatory vertical for the SupTech solution, building on the GTA Qatar mandate.
Build the IRIS Peridot MSME ecosystem in DataTech, supported by lending partnerships and government collaborations, acknowledged as still in its early stages.
Use the liquidity and balance-sheet flexibility created by the TaxTech / GST ASP divestment to invest in core growth areas such as SupTech, RegTech and enterprise SaaS.
Fund product innovation, market expansion and leadership talent from internal resources while maintaining a strong balance sheet, without raising additional resources.

Scale the newly launched RegAI platform, which assimilates regulations across multiple disciplines and analyses narrative and numeric disclosures for compliance conformity, and combine it with IRIS CARBON for enterprise customers.
Achieve AI fluency in the software development and testing process, building on productivity improvements and faster feature releases already observed.

drhp.business: IRIS builds software platforms that convert regulatory compliance and corporate disclosure into structured, machine-readable and increasingly AI-assisted processes. The business is organised across SupTech (digital reporting, data collection, validation and supervisory technology for regulators and public authorities), RegTech (disclosure management, sustainability and structured financial reporting for enterprises, led by the IRIS Carbon platform) and DataTech. Following the strategic divestment of its TaxTech / GST ASP business, the Company is focused on a scalable, product-led model with …
drhp.end_markets: Regulators and public authorities seeking digital reporting, data collection, validation and supervisory technology|Enterprises and financial institutions adopting disclosure management, sustainability and structured financial reporting solutions|International markets, particularly jurisdictions where regulators are moving towards structured data-based reporting systems|India - domestic RegTech market across banks, NBFCs, insurers and fintech companies
drhp.expansion: IRIS is an asset-light software products business, so its expansion is expressed as product build-out, market entry and talent rather than plant or capacity projects; the annual report contains no plant, line or capacity commissioning programme. The defining capital event of FY26 was the divestment of the TaxTech / GST ASP business, undertaken to simplify operations, sharpen focus on core growth areas and strengthen the Company's financial position; management states the proceeds and gains strengthened the balance sheet, improved liquidity and provided additional flexibility to invest in core …

drhp.mdna: Structural shift in which regulation is becoming a data ecosystem: across capital markets, central banks, business registries and tax authorities, periodic form-based reporting is giving way to structured, machine-readable and increasingly real-time data flows.|Supervisory authorities are adopting technology-enabled approaches to reduce oversight lag, improve risk visibility and move towards continuous supervision, increasing demand for SupTech lifecycle platforms.|Enterprises face increasing disclosure obligations across financial, regulatory and sustainability reporting and are seeking …
drhp.one_liner: IRIS RegTech Solutions Limited (formerly IRIS Business Services Limited) is a product-led regulatory technology company operating at the intersection of regulation, reporting and technology, serving regulators through SupTech and enterprises through RegTech and DataTech platforms.

risks.note: Many large financial institutions and supervisory authorities still run fragmented legacy systems, making deployment of modern compliance platforms operationally complex and resource intensive; the report states these integration challenges often impact implementation timelines, interoperability and enterprise-wide scalability - directly affecting revenue recognition timing and project cost for a platform vendor.
risks.risk: Integration with fragmented legacy infrastructure at customers and regulators

risks.note: Inconsistent data quality, fragmented information systems and multi-jurisdictional reporting misalignment are flagged as persistent industry problems that can impact reporting accuracy, automation efficiency and regulatory responsiveness - the exact outcomes IRIS platforms are bought to deliver.
risks.risk: Data quality and interoperability across multi-jurisdiction reporting

risks.note: As AI is embedded into compliance workflows, regulators and enterprises are emphasising auditable, explainable and traceable systems, particularly in high-risk workflows where automated decisions require clear accountability; this raises the product and assurance bar for an AI-led roadmap.

The Board's Report states operating margins moderated versus the prior year mainly due to continued investments in product development, technology, infrastructure, sales and marketing, and talent acquisition to support long-term growth - so revenue growth is not currently translating into operating leverage.
risks.risk: Margin moderation from a sustained investment phase

risks.note: The Board explicitly cautions that the gain on disposal of the TaxTech / GST ASP business is non-recurring in nature and that the Company's underlying operating performance should be viewed separately from the one-time impact of the divestment.
risks.risk: Earnings quality distorted by a one-time divestment gain

risks.note: Exports contributed 81% of total turnover in FY26 and the client base spans 55 countries, with international delivery through subsidiaries in the USA, Singapore, Malaysia and Italy - concentrating the business in cross-border regulatory cycles, currency movements and foreign procurement decisions.

IRIS handles regulatory and disclosure data for regulators, banks and corporates in an environment the report describes as facing rising cyber threats, data breaches and tightening data-governance regimes such as the DPDP Act; the Company mitigates through ISO 27001:2022 and SOC 2 Type II certifications, but a security failure would be reputationally decisive for a compliance vendor.
risks.risk: Data security and privacy obligations on sensitive regulatory data

risks.note: This is the Company's first BRSR, published voluntarily, with several practices described as remaining partial rather than fully operational, Scope 3 emissions based on spend-based estimates, and no external assurance obtained - leaving disclosure quality dependent on future build-out as ESG reporting obligations widen.
risks.risk: Early-stage ESG data and governance maturity
